title: User Manager UI
objective: Permission-bound User Manager screens for users, roles, and groups including per-tenant assignments and the effective-access view (spec FR-13/FR-14, PRD 20.1.1).
scope: Users: list, create (first/last/email + tenant assignment), edit with tabs Profile / Tenants / Roles / Permissions / Groups / Effective access, deactivate flow
Roles: list, create/edit (name + permission picker grouped by category), usage view before disable
Groups: list, create/edit, members management, group roles, group direct permissions
implementation_details: features/userManager/UserListPage.tsx, UserFormPage.tsx (create), UserDetailPage.tsx with tab components; tenant-assignment editor requires >=1 tenant for non-Internal (mirrors backend rule for UX only)
EffectiveAccessTab.tsx rendering direct roles, direct permissions, group memberships, tenant assignments, and resolved permission set per tenant (from GET /users/{id}/effective-access)
RoleFormPage.tsx: permission picker = grouped checkbox tree from GET /permissions; RoleUsageDialog shown before disable listing users/groups
GroupDetailPage.tsx: members table with add/remove (user search), roles multi-select, direct permissions picker
DeactivateUserDialog (danger; restates login block + history retention)
usersApi/rolesApi/groupsApi RTK Query modules with tag invalidation

e2e: user-manager.spec.ts: create role with permissions; create group and assign role; create user assigned to tenant+group; effective access shows inherited permission; deactivated user cannot log in (generic error); role usage dialog lists the group before disable; non-admin sees no User Manager nav

findings.description: FR-13 scope items have no automated verification: group members-management (add/remove), group direct-permissions save, and the UserDetailPage user-edit save path. No component tests exist for GroupDetailPage/UserDetailPage, and the e2e user-manager.spec.ts never exercises the group members table, handleSavePermissions, or UserDetailPage.handleSave (it only checks a role box + Save roles, and opens the effective-access tab). Repo mandate: every requirement must have at least one test with clear pass/fail. Code looks correct on inspection, so this is a small fix.
findings.recommendation: Add focused RTL component tests: (a) GroupDetailPage add member + remove member call the correct group API with correct args and surface a rejected 403 gracefully; (b) GroupDetailPage save-permissions calls the group permissions API with the selected codes; (c) UserDetailPage Save calls updateUser with the assembled full-replace payload. Optionally extend the e2e to touch the group members table once, but component tests satisfy the mandate.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator independent audit). GroupDetailPage.test.tsx (5) asserts addGroupMember(5,11)+table refresh, removeGroupMember(5,10)+table shrink (within group-members-table so not fooled by the re-populated add dropdown), setGroupPermissions(5,[leads.view,parties.view]) with an exact length-2 check (not arrayContaining), and 403 paths asserting the shared toast showError channel with group-detail-page staying mounted. UserDetailPage.test.tsx (4) asserts the exact full-replace updateUser(42,{roleAssignments/permissionAssignments tagged with active tenant id, groupIds, tenantIds}) matching UserDetailPage.tsx:105-113, edited-field propagation, and 403/422 via ErrorBanner (correct, handleSave uses setFormError). Evaluator confirmed the GroupDetailPage toast-showError-not-ErrorBanner claim is accurate real behavior (verified GroupDetailPage.tsx:126-128,138-139,162-163), tested rather than editing working code. Tests fail if wiring were wrong (exact args + refresh assertions depend on loadDetail being called). FR-13 members-management, group-direct-permissions, and user-edit-save each now have a covering test. Component suite 85/85 (was 72; +9 F-048 + 4 oidc).

findings.description: user-manager.spec.ts scenario 2 (no-nav + Forbidden on chained deep links) is flaky: fails 5/5 cold-context / passes warm-serial. Root cause independently confirmed as pre-existing T-013 shell behavior (in-memory-only tokens force a fresh Keycloak silent-auth round trip on full-reload page.goto; app hangs mid /auth/callback ~15s) - the IDENTICAL flake reproduces on the already-PASSED tenant-manager.spec.ts:90, so it is NOT a T-015 regression. But a committed knowingly-flaky e2e is a quality problem.
findings.evidence: user-manager.spec.ts:164-171 (deep-link Forbidden assertions); observed hang at /auth/callback?...code=...; tenant-manager.spec.ts:90 same flake.
findings.recommendation: Before asserting forbidden-page after a deep-link goto, wait for the OIDC callback to settle (e.g. await page.waitForURL(u => !u.pathname.startsWith('/auth/callback')) or an auth-ready signal); ideally add this to the shared e2e auth/nav helper so both user-manager and tenant-manager specs are robust. Separately track the T-013 auth-callback deep-link-return latency as a shell hardening follow-up.
findings.root_cause_update: Fix iteration 2 diagnosis (Implementor, browser-instrumented): the flake is NOT mere latency. Root cause is React <StrictMode> (src/ui/src/main.tsx) double-invoking AuthProvider's login effect on a full-reload deep link -> two concurrent OIDC round trips race -> one token exchange returns 400 -> the SPA sometimes falls back to /overview instead of the deep-linked path, defeating retries. Confirmed precisely: temporarily removing StrictMode (diagnostic, reverted, main.tsx byte-identical) made both user-manager scenario 2 AND tenant-manager's deep-link test pass reliably across 4+ isolated runs. This is a genuine T-013 shell auth-robustness bug (unguarded duplicate concurrent login-effect invocation), reachable by real users on cold deep-link loads. Added gotoAndExpectForbidden helper (e2e_tests/helpers/auth.ts, waits for /auth/callback to settle + bounded retry) used by both specs, but the helper alone cannot fully close this without the shell fix. ORCHESTRATOR DECISION: authorize the T-013 AuthProvider fix (guard the login effect against duplicate concurrent invocation via an in-flight ref) within this fix effort to fully close F-049 and stabilize both e2e specs.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator independent audit incl. security regression check). Fixed at the real root cause in src/ui/src/auth/oidc.ts: module-level in-flight-promise guards on beginLogin (signinRedirect) and completeLogin (signinRedirectCallback), set SYNCHRONOUSLY before any await so StrictMode's same-tick second invocation reuses the same promise (no second competing OIDC round trip / one-shot code re-exchange), cleared via .finally() so a rejection cannot wedge auth and a genuinely-new later login (post-logout/re-auth) is not suppressed. StrictMode STAYS enabled (main.tsx:14 unchanged); AuthProvider.tsx unchanged. SECURITY PRESERVED (evaluator-verified): tokens still in-memory only (InMemoryTokenStore/WebStorageStateStore-in-memory unchanged), PKCE/code flow unchanged, no client secret, signOut unchanged, automaticSilentRenew unchanged, post-login fetchMe->activeTenantId->setSession intact; only new state is two nullable module-level promises, no new persistence/attack surface. oidc.test.ts (4 tests) proves concurrent-collapse, no-suppress-after-settle, shared-rejection. Flake independently confirmed GONE: evaluator ran user-manager deep-link 3/3 + tenant-manager deep-link 3/3 cold-isolation + login/logout/shell 11/11; Implementor ran 5/5 + 3/3. gotoAndExpectForbidden retained as defense-in-depth, no longer load-bearing. Deeper product benefit: closes a real OIDC race reachable by users on cold deep-link loads.

findings.description: permissionCatalog.ts is a static client mirror of PermissionCatalog.All (verified 100% in sync today, 73/73 codes) with no automated guard against future divergence. If the backend catalog changes, the RoleFormPage/PermissionPicker silently drifts (offering a code the backend rejects, or omitting a new code). Acceptable documented interim since T-007 exposes no GET /permissions, but unguarded.
findings.recommendation: Preferred: add a small backend GET /permissions endpoint sourced from PermissionCatalog.All (code+category+description) and fetch it in the picker (module already structured for a drop-in swap). Acceptable alternative if the endpoint contract is contentious: add a drift-guard test that fails when the client mirror diverges from the backend catalog. Non-blocking.
findings.resolution: Verified fix iteration 2 (evaluator independent audit). Closed via the acceptable-alternative drift-guard: src/api/tests/QuoteIQ.Domain.Tests/Security/PermissionCatalogDriftGuardTests.cs resolves the client permissionCatalog.ts via [CallerFilePath] (repo-root path arithmetic verified), extracts codes with a regex matching the file's { code: '...' } shape, and asserts equality BOTH directions (missingFromClient AND extraInClient), so a code added to either side fails CI. Evaluator confirmed the drift-guard-over-new-endpoint reasoning holds (PermissionCatalog.All is an in-process static list never surfaced over HTTP; wiring GET /permissions through 3 pickers + mocks is materially larger blast radius than the informational-catalog drift risk). Risk genuinely closed; test passes (Domain 10/10).

Evaluation (iteration 1/10): VERDICT NEEDS_FIXES. SECURITY PASS (no high/critical/major): RouteGuard Forbidden + nav hidden are UX-only, every fetch hits a RequirePermission endpoint, ceiling is a disabled-checkbox affordance only with server 403 surfaced inline (real test), no XSS/secrets. Deviation adjudications: static catalog mirror 100% in sync today (73/73) - acceptable interim but unguarded (F-050 minor); tenant-options-from-session correct (backend authoritative, minor nuance for global callers). Deep-link flake INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED pre-existing T-013 OIDC full-reload root cause (fails 5/5 cold, passes warm-serial; identical flake reproduced on already-PASSED tenant-manager.spec.ts:90) - not a T-015 regression, does not block on its own (F-049 minor).
